children: shares slipped 3% in extended trading on Tuesday as the PC peripherals company reported third-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's forecast.

For the period ending Sept. 30, Logitech said it earned an adjusted $1.51 per share as revenue rose 2.5% year-over-year to $1.22B. Analysts had expected the company, which makes headsets, keyboards, and more, to earn an adjusted $1.33 per share on $1.21B in revenue.
"We delivered our eleventh consecutive quarter of growth and launched 19 new products for the holiday quarter," said Hanneke Faber, Logitech CEO, in a
. "Growth in the Americas, Video Collaboration and Gaming supported our topline growth. Our strategic priorities and operational discipline continue to deliver."
Looking to the fiscal third-quarter, Logitech expects sales to be between $1.36B and $1.43B, with adjusted operating income between $220M and $255M. Analysts had expected $1.3B in revenue.
The company will host a conference call at 4:30 p.m. EST to discuss the results.

title: Logitech slips even as consumers keep buying PC peripherals
